agentCan: Author the FDK app configuration (oauth_config.json, requests.json, manifest.json) and request templates
Build and test locally with fdk run
Implement the reauthorize UX for refresh-token expiry

approval.cost: No submission/listing fee is stated in the docs read; paid Marketplace apps exist and monetization is governed by the Marketplace Terms of Use ('Charges, Collection, Revenue Share, and Payment' sections), whose actual percentages are not in the developer docs read
approval.trigger: The OAuth credentials themselves require no review (self-service in the Developer Portal), and a Custom app 'is not subject to review; it is available for installation as soon as it is submitted and published'. But a public Marketplace ('Freshworks app') listing requires full Freshworks review before publication, tracked in five per-category steps: Code ('Code quality, security, and platform compliance'), QA ('Functional testing'), Content ('Listing content, links, category, screenshots, video, and descriptions'), Security ('Security and privacy review'), and Business ('Business and marketplace policy review'). Overall statuses run Draft/In Development, Under Review, Changes requested / Ready to publish, Published (or Rejected). External apps (listed in the Marketplace but installed from your own URL) also require review ('Review Required: Yes'). No pre-approval user/install caps are stated; the practical gate is binary: an unapproved Marketplace app is not published, so no customers can install it from the Marketplace. After publication you may hide the app from the gallery and share an account-specific URL for selective access.
approval.wait: Not stated (no review turnaround or SLA published in the docs read)

blockers.detail: 'The refresh token has a lifetime of 365 days. After the refresh token expires, the access token is not updated and all REST API calls fail with a 401 - Unauthorized error.' Recovery is human: front-end agent apps must show a Reauthorize button; for serverless/account-level apps the admin must reauthorize from the App Gallery Settings page. Also: 'When a user is deleted from an organization or removed from an account, the authorization server revokes any consents given to OAuth apps in that account and delete the refresh tokens issued to those apps.'
blockers.howToClear: Calendar the 365-day cliff per connection, monitor for 401s, and build the reauthorize path before you need it.
blockers.title: 365-day refresh-token death forces a human back in

blockers.detail: 'While you can add new scopes, removing scopes that are already selected is not supported' when updating OAuth credentials. And 'the mapping between OAuth apps and OAuth credentials is 1-1. A configured OAuth credential can only be used with one app': reusing credentials in a second published app errors in the App Management Portal.
blockers.howToClear: Choose scopes conservatively at creation (you can add later, never remove) and create separate credentials per app.
blockers.title: Scopes can be added, never removed; credentials are 1:1 with apps

blockers.detail: Endpoints are per-organization (https://<freshworks org domain>/oauth/v2/authorize), with no single global authorize host. If you hardcode the org domain in authorize_url/token_url and the customer's org domain changes (e.g. account transfer), 'the app users will face an error while authenticating', and fixing it requires releasing a new app version. The docs direct you to capture the domain via oauth_iparams at install time.
blockers.howToClear: Capture the org domain via oauth_iparams at install; never hardcode it.
blockers.title: Never hardcode the org domain

flavor.recommended: Freshworks OAuth credentials with token_type 'account' (one admin authorization per customer account)
flavor.why: The object is a set of OAuth credentials registered in the Freshworks Developer Portal (Settings > OAuth Credentials > Create OAuth Credentials), generating a Client ID and Client Secret. token_type flavors: 'account' ('Authorization handshake is initiated only when an admin installs the app') vs 'agent' ('initiated when an agent installs the app'). Only one OAuth configuration per app may be agent-level, and token_type cannot be 'agent' for serverless or background apps. The documented flow is built primarily around Freshworks (FDK) apps installed into Freshsales accounts.

humanMust: Create a Freshworks Developer account and the OAuth credentials in the Developer Portal
Record the Client ID and Client Secret at creation
The customer's admin (account flavor) or agent (agent flavor) clicks Authorize at install
Submit the app for Marketplace review if you want a public listing; reauthorize connections when refresh tokens die
name: Freshsales
nuances: Access tokens live 30 minutes, and for FDK apps the developer platform refreshes for you ('the developer platform places a refresh-access-token call to the authorization server and regenerates the access token').

Registration fields have quirks: the app Name must be 'a name not exceeding 3 words' and, with Description, is shown to users in the authorization window; up to a maximum of five redirect URLs are allowed.

Platform caps: v3.0 apps may access a maximum of three OAuth-secured resources; v3.1+ a maximum of five; multi-account authorization supports 'up to 20 accounts per OAuth-secured resource' (account-level only).
Agent-flavor ceilings: agent-level OAuth is unavailable to serverless/background apps and cannot be invoked from server.js (only via $credentials.oauth for account-level configs).

Documentation skew: the OAuth documentation lives in the Freshworks app-platform (FDK) docs and is written around front-end/serverless/SMI apps; the standalone use of these org OAuth endpoints by a wholly external web service is not walked through step-by-step. Freshsales REST API rate limit on the API-key route: 1000 requests per hour per account (429 on breach).
prerequisites: A Freshworks Developer account and Developer Portal access
App Name (max 3 words), Description, Redirect URL(s) (max five), and scope selections (product, then per-resource permission checkboxes, producing scopes like freshsales.deals.view)
For FDK testing: the FDK CLI (fdk run) and the local callback http://localhost:10001/auth/callback

steps.detail: Create a Freshworks Developer account and sign in to the Developer Portal with your organization/account URL.
steps.title: Create a Freshworks Developer account

steps.detail: Settings (gear icon) > OAuth Credentials > Create OAuth Credentials: Name (mandatory, max 3 words, shown in the authorization window), Description (mandatory, also shown), Redirect URL(s) (mandatory, up to five), and scopes (pick product(s), then per-resource permission checkboxes). Click Create Credentials and record the Client ID and Client Secret.
steps.title: Create the OAuth credentials

steps.detail: Put the credentials into config/oauth_config.json (client_id, client_secret, authorize_url, token_url, options.scope, options.customHeaders.Authorization as Base64 of client_id:client_secret, token_type 'account', plus oauth_iparams to capture the customer's org domain at install time). Declare request templates in config/requests.json and reference them in manifest.json.
steps.title: Configure the app

steps.detail: Build with fdk run, install the app from the Custom Apps section of the customer's Freshsales Marketplace Apps gallery, and click Authorize to run the handshake. For FDK apps 'the developer platform constructs the authorization-code request' and the Marketplace constructs the access-token request and stores the access and refresh tokens.
steps.title: Build and test locally

steps.detail: Access tokens live 30 minutes (the platform refreshes automatically for FDK apps); refresh tokens live 365 days, after which all calls fail with 401 until a human reauthorizes. Plan account-level caps: max 3 OAuth-secured resources on v3.0 apps, 5 on v3.1+; up to 20 accounts per resource.
steps.title: Run with 30-minute access tokens and a 365-day refresh cliff

steps.detail: Choose the distribution: Custom app (no review, installable as soon as submitted and published), External app (review required), or Marketplace/Freshworks app (full five-category review: Code, QA, Content, Security, Business; statuses from Under Review through Changes requested / Ready to publish to Published or Rejected).
steps.title: Distribute (Custom, External, or Marketplace)

tagline: Real OAuth 2.0 run at the Freshworks platform level: credentials are self-service and Custom apps skip review entirely, but a public Marketplace listing faces a five-category review with no stated turnaround, and every connection carries a hard 365-day refresh-token expiry.

time.active: ~30 min of credential/app configuration + FDK build time
time.total: Same day for Custom apps; Marketplace publication waits on a review with no stated duration
